payload.blocks: Which session drives phases 5 and 7 of the Windows custody plan. Nothing breaks while it waits: this session has stopped acting, and the other lead keeps going.
payload.headline: Two leads run the Windows custody plan: stop this restarted one, or the other?

parts.cause: The supervisor restarted the lead head while the earlier lead session was still active. A lead may not start or stop sessions, and it has no channel to the supervisor except this question.

options.does: The supervisor stops head:lead-forgent-261121-1309-git-wi-2454d (this session). The other lead fixes the scan finding in phase 5 or 7 from the report.
options.gain: No disruption: the lead that landed phase 4 and holds phase 5's state keeps going.
options.harm: The scan fix depends on the other lead reading the report.
options.label: Stop this restarted lead

options.cost: One stop plus re-reading phase 5's state.
options.does: The supervisor stops the other session. This session picks up phase 5 from 1bdb14fd4, fixes the scan, then runs phase 7.
options.gain: The session that found the scan bug owns the fix.
options.harm: It throws away the other lead's in-flight context and any unit it is running.
options.label: Stop the other lead

parts.recommendation: Stop this restarted lead. The other session is ahead (it landed phase 4 and rebased phase 5); send it the review report.

scope.allows: Stopping one of the two lead sessions of this plan and routing the scan finding to the lead that remains.
scope.forbids: Changing the plan footprint or the phase order.

parts.what: This lead session restarted at 17:51 and resumed the plan. Meanwhile another session landed phase 4 (9852d8c97, 18:03) and rebased and pushed wincustody/p5 (1bdb14fd4). That is two leads on one plan. A review this session ran also found the landed Windows C5 scan fails open: in workspace-only mode a same-user process whose cwd cannot be read (elevated or 32-bit) is not counted, so git-wal-v1 can be admitted while an old writer is alive. Details are in plans/261121-1309-git-windows-custody/reports/lead-261121-1805-windows-scan-review.md.
